correctness.rationale: Independently recursed over every ordered exponent composition of 5 and strictly increasing odd primes <=383, with rational exact I(p^a)=σ(p^a)/p^a and admissible monotone prefix upper bounds. Obtained exactly 121 abundant values, smallest 945, largest 442365; first/tail integers matched the claimed families and independent OEIS A287646 table. For unbounded primes the source proves a separate extremal upper bound for largest prime >=389 across all support sizes r<=5, so q<=383 is exhaustive; Ω<=4 extremal 3·5·7·11 ratio=2304/1155<2; no finite cutoff used as unexplained infinite fact.

evidence: If Ω(n)=5 and n is odd abundant, every proper divisor d has Ω(d)<5 and is deficient, so n is primitive abundant.
A primitive abundant n is abundant by definition. Hence the row n=5 of A287646 comprises exactly all odd abundant Ω=5, nothing less.

originality.rationale: OEIS A287646, authored M. F. Hasler on 2017-05-30, explicitly provides the entire row for odd PRIMITIVE abundant numbers with Ω=5, and linked A287728 states row length 121, start 945 and end 442365. Every odd abundant integer with Ω=5 is automatically primitive abundant because no odd number with Ω<=4 is abundant. Therefore the existing exact row is IDENTICAL to the claimed entire first Ω=5 abundant set; its full enumeration algorithm is already given. The ten compact prime families merely reformat known exact elements, not a previously unknown classification.
residual_risks: The ten compressed prime-factor range families might be a convenient representation but do not change equivalence to the pre-existing full table.
No repair attempted: rewriting a covered list as prime-parametric families without a new substantive invariant cannot establish originality.

value.rationale: The mathematical task of an exact first odd-abundant layer is natural, but the final scientific deliverable solely re-enumerates a 121-member layer tabulated with a general all-rows enumeration algorithm in OEIS since 2017. Repackaging a known list as ten prime support ranges is an unmotivated presentation gain without a new structural theorem, so it falls under known-table recomputation rather than a valuable independent unknown invariant.

final_claim: Complete classification of odd abundant integers with total prime multiplicity Ω(n)=5 as ten listed prime-power/range families, exactly 121 integers between 945 and 442365; no odd abundant with Ω<=4.
limitations: Prior exact 121-term OEIS table means source claim is covered; additional numerical certificate cannot rescue originality.
